text:
Arjun Patel: FYI ran a 6h fleet saturation sim using the proposed token-accounting change (per-GPU buckets + token-weighted requests). Results look concerning — TPM throttles spike even though overall GPU util is <95%. Queueing grows nonlinearly when a small subset of long sequences hit at once.

Maya Chen: Can you paste the sim numbers? was this with the current admission control parameters?

Arjun Patel: Ran two runs: baseline and per-gpu-token-bucket. Key diffs below:
```
Baseline: GPUs avg util 86%, tail queue 1.2k, throttled reqs 2.3%
Per-GPU token-bucket: GPUs avg util 92%, tail queue 8.1k, throttled tokens 18%
Note: workload mix = 70% short chat (mean 48 tok), 30% long completions (mean 1.6k tok) arriving in bursts (Poisson+bursts)
```

Ben Liu: Interesting. Sounds like the token-bucket split created hotspots where a few GPUs get many long sequences and exhaust their local buckets while others are underutilized. Did you try allowing cross-GPU borrowing or global overflow?

Arjun Patel: Yes. I simulated two borrowing policies: soft-borrow (borrow up to 25% of neighbor bucket) and global-leaky (fall back to global bucket when local empty). Soft-borrow improved tail queue to ~3.4k but increased coordination latency. Global-leaky nearly matched baseline throttling but raised cross-node traffic by ~12% (more KV cache misses).

Priya Kapoor: Do we have the admission-control rules currently tied to user TPM or to fleet capacity? IIRC we map customer TPM -> admission tokens but not to per-GPU fill state.

Arjun Patel: Current prod maps per-customer rate -> admission queue weight, then scheduler places requests by normal load balancing. We don't decrement per-GPU token counters until the request is scheduled — that's part of the problem: scheduling decisions don't consider token budgets at placement time.

Maya Chen: So scheduler places a long request onto a node that appears free, then that node's token bucket is emptyed and starts throttling, while other nodes could have handled it. That's rough. Two ideas: (1) make admission control aware of per-node token budgets at placement time (cheap), (2) weighted routing that prefers nodes with >X% token headroom for large token requests.

Ben Liu: Agreed on both. Also suggest we change accounting from 'requests' to 'token-weighted units' for admission tokens. Right now a single short request and a 2k-token request consume equal admission slots in some parts of the stack, which skews SLOs.

Arjun Patel: I prototyped a token-weighted admission bucket. Config snippet used in sim:
```
{
  "admission": {
    "global_tpm": 600000,
    "per_gpu_bucket_refill_tpm": 30000,
    "burst_scale": 2,
    "token_weighting": "tokens",
    "large_request_threshold_tokens": 512,
    "placement_headroom_pct": 20
  }
}
```
Applying token weighting reduced unfairness: throttled tokens dropped from 18% -> 6%, tail queue from 8.1k -> 2.2k. But it increased short-request latency 8-12ms due to tighter global guards.

Priya Kapoor: What's the cost impact? shifting to token accounting might reduce wasted GPU cycles but may inflate API-side admission rejections (customer experience). Need rollback plan.

Arjun Patel: Quick cost estimate from sim logs: net token processing decreased ~5% fleet-wide (less wasted model runs due to early admission rejects). But customer-visible rejections up ~0.6% for free-tierish short bursts. For paid customers with reserved capacity, we can reserve a small explicit short-request slice to avoid hurting PLG funnel.

sre-bot: [alert] simulated a scenario where node 12 enters token exhaustion loop -> autoscaler couldn't spin up compatible slot because placement respects data-locality. Consider relaxing locality for overflow in emergency.

Maya Chen: Action items I propose:
- Arjun: open a PR with the token-weighted admission prototype for eng-infra review (include sim results + config).
- Ben: prototype scheduler check to prefer nodes with placement_headroom_pct and measure added latency for placement decision.
- Priya: draft a short rollback/communication plan for customers if we flip the switch (esp reserved vs free).
- SRE: add a short-circuit that allows global overflow with a cost tag if node-local buckets are empty and global has headroom.

Ben Liu: Also let's add a metric: "tokens_throttled_by_node" and per-request token_cost tag so we can debug hot nodes without digging through traces.

Arjun Patel: I'll drop the sim artifacts & CSV into the eng-infra drive and open the PR today. cc @Maya Chen @Ben Liu @Priya Kapoor. Thanks all :rocket:
